..
Satellite imagery depicts isolated thunderstorms and locally heavy 
showers in a north-to-south oriented axis along the Marianas. The 
convective activity began in the far northern Marianas this morning 
and has backfilled southward along a train of showers as the day 
progressed. A subtropical ridge has set up to the northeast, 
advecting drier air which will push off the convection to the west 
over the western and southern coastal waters of Tinian and Saipan in 
the early evening. As for Rota and Guam, the convective activity is 
not expected to subside until after midnight when the drier air 
completely envelops the region, bringing partly cloudy skies and 
isolated showers for the Marianas early Friday morning through Friday
night. The trades are expected to increase as the ridge continues to
intensify, so breezy winds and scattered showers are a possibility 
around early next week.

Marine...
Buoy and altimetry data shows combined seas of 3 to 5 feet which 
will remain in the forecast until the trade swell quickly builds in 
starting late Saturday afternoon, possibly peaking to 6 to 8 feet 
early next week. There is a moderate risk of rip currents along 
north- and east-facing reefs through the rest of the week. Along 
with the building swell, surf may increase along east-facing reefs 
that may warrant a high risk of rip currents, but may not exceed 
hazardous criteria. We will continue to monitor the sea state once 
the weekend nears.

Eastern Micronesia...
After a short burst of convective activity overnight near Pohnpei and
Majuro, a fairly moderate trade-wind regime is expected to return to
the region, bringing on-and-off showers and some thunderstorms for
the rest of the forecast period. The likelihood of any significant
tropical development continues to decrease as most of the convection
is expected to sit either along 10N, or along the Equator over at 
least the next several days. 

Combined seas of 4 to 6 feet in Pohnpei and Kosrae waters, and 5 to 
7 feet in Majuro waters, are expected to increase another foot or two
by the weekend as trade swell and localized wind waves strengthen. 
This will allow some of the seas to intrude into the aforementioned 
waters, but sea conditions will remain below levels hazardous to 
small craft for the time being.

Western Micronesia...
A weakening ridge across far western Micronesia is maintaining light
winds across Yap and Palau, with only patchy showers seen across the
area. Island-effect showers are still possible for Palau Friday
afternoon, before winds increase to light to moderate across Yap and
Palau through the weekend. Farther east, scattered showers are 
beginning to build into Chuuk along an area of weak trade-wind 
convergence. Latest model guidance is less keen on an weak tropical 
disturbance developing, however, a band of trade-wind convergence or
an ITCZ fragment still looks to develop across Chuuk, southern Yap 
State, and the far southern islands of Palau over the next few days. 
Fresh to strong trades north of this feature and an embedded trough, 
will support a more unsettled pattern across Chuuk Friday through at 
least Saturday night, before this feature shifts northwest. For Yap 
and Palau, a series of weak trade-wind troughs will bring periodic 
upticks in showers over the next several days, then the shift in the 
developing pattern near Chuuk may also result in a broader area of 
scattered showers building into Yap early next week. 

Overall, benign marine conditions are expected over the next several
days. Altimetry data shows combined seas of 3 to 5 feet across the
region. A building trade swell is expected to increase seas to 4 to 
6 feet at Chuuk starting Friday and at Yap around Sunday and Monday. 
For Palau, seas look to remain around 2 to 4 feet through much of the
upcoming week.
